errors.english: whether a (Mimamsaka) a follower of the Mimamsa school of Hindu philosophy or another commentator
errors.why: rgyal dpog pa is the proper name Jaimini (author of the Mīmāṃsāsūtra), not a generic 'Mimamsaka'; the same misrendering recurs later in 'like a (Mimamsaka)' and 'is a (Mimamsaka) and so forth'.

fix.find: whether a (Mimamsaka) a follower of the Mimamsa school of Hindu philosophy or another commentator

errors.english: If one relies on scripture for a meaning that is extremely hidden
errors.why: The Tibetan says that if, for extremely hidden objects, scripture depends on non-deception established by another pramāṇa; the dependence on another pramāṇa is dropped.

errors.english: In that case, it is not accepted that the one who knows the meaning is a (Mimamsaka) and so forth; however, if it is through inference [note: term: anumana], then who would fall into this fault?
errors.why: This is the opponent's objection: 'we do not hold that Jaimini and others know it by perception but by inference, so by what would this fault arise?'; the English garbles it and does not mark it as the opponent's view.

note: The argument against Mīmāṃsā is broadly followed, but Jaimini is turned into a school label and the opponent's inference objection is garbled.

errors.english: the notion that many objects of knowledge are properties
errors.why: shes pa here means cognitions (the many consciousnesses just mentioned), not objects of knowledge.

fix.find: the notion that many objects of knowledge are properties
fix.replace: the notion that many cognitions are properties

note: A sound rendering of the refutation of the elements as the basis of mind, with one term slip.
Faithful rendering of Bhāviveka's reply on the fire example and the gone/not-gone/being-traversed argument; verses correctly set off.

errors.english: if that which is empty of appearances is another property, it would be equivalent to and indeed become the (hetu) logical reason or evidence itself
errors.why: der snang is 'the semblance of that [reason]' (hetvābhāsa): the verse says that if the reason is a property devoid of pseudo-reasons, another property would equally become a reason; 'empty of appearances' loses the point.
drug pa here most likely refers to the sixth grammatical case (case-ending of the definition), not a sixth ontological category.

note: Follows the critique of Nyāya and Vaiśeṣika definitions of the reason, but the opening verse and some logical terms are blurred.

errors.english: Having made the thesis that "essence is empty,"
errors.why: The thesis (begun on the previous side with dngos po thams cad) is that all entities are empty of own-nature, not that essence is empty.

fix.find: Having made the thesis that "essence is empty,"
fix.replace: Having made the thesis that [all entities] "are empty of essence,"

note: Good rendering of Avalokitavrata's gloss on disputing by means of emptiness, with the MMK 1.1 verse correctly set; the opening thesis is misstated.

errors.english: the tenth (saṅghāvaśeṣa) formal meeting of the monastic community
errors.why: dge 'dun lhag ma is the saṅghāvaśeṣa class of offence; this marks the end of the tenth saṅghāvaśeṣa rule, not a 'formal meeting'.

fix.find: the tenth (saṅghāvaśeṣa) formal meeting of the monastic community

note: Accurate Vinaya commentary on the schism-supporter rule, including the duṣkṛta/sthūlātyaya gradation, apart from mislabeling saṅghāvaśeṣa.

errors.english: The opponent argues: "From the familiarity of others," and so forth.
errors.why: gzhan gyi marks the words as the opponent's (as elsewhere on the side); the quoted reply is simply 'from familiarity', not 'the familiarity of others'.

fix.find: The opponent argues: "From the familiarity of others," and so forth.
fix.replace: The opponent says: "From familiarity," and so forth.

errors.english: When one sees the fire and its burning one line of text follows
errors.why: 'one line of text follows' is not in the Tibetan, which only says 'when fire and the like are seen, burning ...' continuing on the next side.

fix.find: When one sees the fire and its burning one line of text follows
fix.replace: When one sees fire and the like, burning

errors.english: Others, thinking that the experienced object cannot be denied, show the sequence
errors.why: It is the commentator who, reasoning that others cannot deny what is experienced, shows the sequence of activity; 'others' are not the ones who show it.

note: The dialectic on pramāṇa and attainment is mostly followed, but speaker markers are misread and a stray artifact ends the page.

errors.english: Then it would be tenable to be both a god and a human.
errors.why: Only the first two lines are MMK 27.16 verse; this sentence is the commentary's prose continuation, but it is set as a third verse line.

note: Clear rendering of the continuum argument and the reply that the reason is stated generally.

errors.english: who sever the hopeless despair of living beings
errors.why: re thag gcod pa is 'to cut off hope', i.e. the departing Sage leaves beings without hope, the opposite of severing their despair.

note: A fluent and largely faithful rendering of the lament verses.

errors.english: because the sprout is what is produced, the sprout is the agent
errors.why: The Tibetan says the sprout is the agent because it is the sprout that arises (as Devadatta is agent of walking), not because it is what is produced.

note: Sound rendering of the ṭīkā's word-glosses on simultaneity of seed and sprout, with one slip on the agent rationale.
